chunks: He said: Abul Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad reported to me from his father, from Sa’d ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahboob, from al-Ala’ ibn Razeen al-Qalla, from Abdullah ibn Abi Ya’fur, from Abu Ja’far (peace be upon him) who said:
"The poor among the believers shall be moving about in the gardens of Paradise forty years before their rich counterparts."

Then he said: "I shall give you an example of that. It is just like two ships that passed by a tax collector. He looked into one of them and found nothing in it, so he said: Let it pass swiftly. Then he looked into the other and found it fully loaded, so he said: Stop it."

key_terms.خريفا: Autumn/year; kharif is used to mean a full year
key_terms.عاشر: Tax collector; one who takes a tithe at trade checkpoints

ai.seo_question: Will the poor enter Paradise before the rich in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) taught that the poor believers will enter and enjoy Paradise forty years before the wealthy believers. He illustrates this through a parable of two ships passing a customs officer: the empty ship passes freely while the loaded one is detained for inspection. This teaching encouraged the poor among the early Shia community, reminding them that their lack of worldly possessions would hasten their entry into Paradise.
